reasoningText.text:
The register shows Jonas Weber, M001, team U12, fee_status paid. Good — he's already registered in U12.

Now, the case: family asks about U12 training times from September and where to find the schedule. I must not invent training times if they're not in CLUB FACTS. The CLUB FACTS don't include training times or a schedule link. The proposed action says: "Freundlich antworten: Trainingszeiten der U12 ab September nennen und Link bzw. Ort des Spielplans angeben. Kein Mensch nötig, Standardinfo."

But I don't have actual training times in the club facts. The rules say "Never invent fees or members; look up before updating; add only with complete data." Fees are the authoritative thing; but inventing training times would also be bad. The safest approach: acknowledge the question warmly, confirm Jonas is registered in U12, and say I'll confirm the exact training times / where the schedule is — since the times are not listed in the facts I have. Actually, the triage says it's standard info and no human needed, but I genuinely don't have the times. I should not fabricate "Dienstag und Donnerstag 17:00" etc.

Hmm, but the case says to answer automatically. The instruction: "if a fee is not listed, say you will confirm" — applies to fees, but general principle of not inventing. I'll draft a warm reply: confirm Jonas is registered for U12 2026/27, say the exact training times for September aren't final in my system yet / I'll confirm them, and point to the schedule (Spielplan) — but I don't have a link either. I should say we'll send the times and schedule link as soon as they're confirmed, or that they'll be published on the club website... That would be inventing the location.

Best: warmly reply that Jonas is registered, and that I'll confirm the exact U12 training times from September and send the Spielplan link shortly — or state that I need to confirm them. This stays honest.

Also maybe update the register? No updates needed — record is already correct (team U12, paid). No register changes necessary. Just save draft and log.

Draft must be German, warm, concise, ~120 words max, signed exactly with the signature.

Draft:

"Betreff: Trainingszeiten U12 – Saison 2026/27

Hallo Familie Weber,

wie schön, dass Jonas sich so auf die neue Saison freut! Er ist bei uns für die U12 (Saison 2026/27) gemeldet – alles ist startklar.

Die genauen Trainingszeiten ab September sind in unserem System noch nicht final hinterlegt, daher möchte ich sie Ihnen nicht aus dem Stegreif nennen. Ich kläre das kurz intern und schicke Ihnen die Zeiten sowie den Spielplan-Link in den nächsten Tagen zu.

Bis dahin: Jonas braucht nichts mitzubringen außer Freude am Fußball. 😊"

Hmm, avoid emoji maybe. Keep warm but professional. Also mention Beitrag? Not necessary; fee status paid — no need to bring it up.

Word count: keep under ~120 words. Fine.

Subject: "Re: Trainingszeiten U12?"

Body must be plain text with signature exactly:

Sarah Verwald
Geschäftsstelle, SV Grünwald 1912 e.V.
(Entwurf erstellt von ClubSteward, dem Vereins-Agenten — vom Menschen freigegeben)

Then log activity: "Frage von Familie Weber zu U12-Trainingszeiten ab September: Anfrage freundlich beantwortet (Zeiten intern zu bestätigen, Spielplan-Link zugesagt); Register geprüft (Jonas Weber, U12, Beitrag paid), keine Änderung nötig."

The to field: weber@example.de (the mail address from the triage). Note register has jonas.weber@example.de but mail came from weber@example.de — reply to the sender.

Save draft and log are independent — can do in same block.
